proposals.evidence: DEDR4616 explicitly gives Tamil makaḷ daughter, Malayalam mōḷ, Kota mōḷ, Kannada magaḷ, Tulu magaḷu, Parji māl and Gadaba māl. The selected survey makaḷ/magaḷ and shortened maka/maga/maha forms are comparative daughter extensions, with southern k/g/h variation and loss of final lateral; Parji/Gadaba māl/malu/melu preserve the separately documented central-Dravidian shape. Source gender/sense and vowel notation are retained; compounds and opaque contractions remain unassigned. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3582 gives Tamil naṭa, Malayalam naṭakka, Kannada naḍe/naḍi, Kodagu naḍa- and Tulu naḍapuni to walk. These complete southern survey naḍa/naḍi/naḍakk-/naḍap- forms preserve the stem and source inflection; the Kudiya naḍapu comparison follows intransitive Tulu naḍapuni, not Kannada causative naḍapu. Longer or opaque responses are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

Selected survey paḷam/payam/pagam/paśam/pām- responses preserve lect-specific reflexes or loss of the medial retroflex, and Kannada/related annu reflects loss of initial h-. These are comparative family proposals; the separate Indo-Aryan-looking phal forms and opaque responses are excluded. proposals.evidence: DEDR1184 explicitly gives Tamil kaṇṇi rope/neckrope, Kannada kaṇṇi rope/cord and Kota kayṇ yokerope. These simple southern survey kaṇṇi/kanni and Irula kəinni rope responses match the documented rope noun, with retroflex/gemination/vowel spelling retained; no eye-word parent is substituted. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
